conviction_note: The externally observable demand proxy for SPWH's exact fiscal Q2 (May+Jul 2026 NSSF-adjusted NICS, +7.7% YoY) accelerated 5.4 points from its fiscal Q1 (+2.3%, when SPWH comped +2.1% with hunting/shooting +7.4%), and two independent supply-side prints (Ruger 29 Jul, Olin Winchester 30 Jul) corroborate real unit and ammunition pull-through, against a company guide of -1% to +2% comps reaffirmed on 2 June and a 3-estimate consensus that models no YoY improvement; I haircut that to +4.0 net because this quarter laps a 32.0% gross margin, because the Q1 comp beat on 2 June moved the stock only +2.11%, and because with 23 contracts of open interest there is no chain to tell me what is actually priced.

findings.finding: NSSF-adjusted NICS for SPWH's exact fiscal Q2 window (May 1,105,758 / June 1,123,006 / July 1,061,883 = 3,290,647 vs 3,055,402 a year earlier, +7.7%) accelerated 5.4 points from the ~+2.3% of its fiscal Q1 (Feb +3.5%, Mar +1.9%, Apr +1.6%), the quarter in which SPWH printed +2.1% comps and +7.4% hunting-and-shooting.
findings.why_not_priced: The July NICS release (5 Aug), Ruger's Q2 call (7 Aug) and Olin's Q2 release (30 Jul) all landed inside the baseline's 20-day window, and the baseline's 20-day run-up is +3.04% of which +3.95% is the last five days alone - i.e. the tape was flat or down through the exact days the sector data printed, and the small gain is pre-earnings drift. If this were priced, the 3-estimate consensus would sit above the company's reaffirmed -1%/+2% comp guide instead of at ($0.11) vs ($0.12) a year ago (no YoY improvement), and a $45m equity levered on $148.4m of net debt would not have absorbed a 5-point acceleration in its primary demand driver for a 3% drift. There is no transmission mechanism: ~276k shares/day (~$330k notional), 3 estimates, 23 contracts of total option open interest.
findings.independence: Two supply-side sources, neither derived from NICS: Sturm Ruger's Q2 2026 release (29 Jul 2026) reports estimated sell-through from distributors to retailers +19% YoY with distributor inventories DOWN 45,800 units and finished-goods down 100,100 units - https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729922943/en/Sturm-Ruger-Company-Inc.-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results ; and Olin's Q2 2026 release (30 Jul 2026) shows Winchester sales $500.3m vs $447.6m (+11.8%) with segment earnings up on 'higher commercial ammunition pricing AND volume' - https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/olin-announces-second-quarter-2026-results-302839441.html . Caveat I could not close: NFA (suppressor) checks are up 108.8% in July and 177% in June after the $200 transfer tax was removed, and I could not verify from NSSF methodology whether NFA sits inside the adjusted series, so some of the +7.7% may be a category SPWH monetises only as a drop-ship referral. Ruger's unit sell-through and Winchester's ammo volume are NFA-independent and are why I still size this positive.

findings.finding: This quarter laps the highest gross margin SPWH has posted in the recent run - 32.0% in Q2 FY2025 - while the Q1 FY2026 it just reported came in at 29.6% (down 80bps YoY) with management attributing the contraction specifically to mix into lower-margin firearms and ammunition, which is precisely the category the NICS acceleration drives.
findings.why_not_priced: The market has the 32.0% number, but the reaction function is the unpriced part: on 2 June 2026 SPWH beat with +2.1% comps and +2.8% sales and the stock moved +2.11%, because gross margin fell 80bps on exactly this mix. So a top-line-only beat is worth roughly nothing on this name, and the difference between a +4% print and a +12% print is entirely whether the 32.0% lap is held and the $30-36m FY EBITDA guide is raised. If the market had focused on this, the 5-day drift would not be positive into a quarter whose margin comparison is its hardest of the year. This is the reason my net number is +4.0 rather than +6.0.
findings.independence: Shares one document with finding 1 - the Q1 FY2026 earnings release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001132105/000119312526253505/spwh-ex99_pr120722.htm, 2026-06-02) supplies both the +7.4% hunting/shooting comp used above and the 29.6%/-80bps mix explanation used here; treat the two as one source cluster. The independent leg here is the Q2 FY2025 release's 32.0% gross margin (URL above) and the reaffirmed FY2026 guide of -1%/+2% comps and $30-36m adjusted EBITDA against FY2025 actual adjusted EBITDA of $27.5m - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1132105/000119312526134574/spwh-ex99_pr120722.htm (2026-03-31).

findings.finding: The 8-K filed 24 June 2026 amended and restated both facilities out to 18 June 2031 - the $45m ABL term loan and a revolver cut from $350m to $315m - so the near-term maturity wall the price appears to embed is gone, and Q1 liquidity was $116.7m against a minimum-availability covenant of the greater of $30m or 10% of the gross borrowing base.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the one place where I think the baseline's forward distribution is wrong rather than the mean: the -29.8% print of 2025-12-04 that anchors the 14.1% median reaction was a distress-tail event on a company with a live maturity and covenant question, and that mechanism is now five years out with $116.7m of headroom. The stock is still within 5.8% of its 52-week low and did not re-rate on the amendment - a 3% stub of enterprise value should move multiples of the observed 3.04% drift if a five-year term-out were being capitalised. I size it at only +1.0 because the refinancing did get wire coverage (TipRanks, TradingView, Globe and Mail) in late June, so this is a statement about the left tail of this print, not about its mean.
findings.independence: Confirmed independently by the Q1 FY2026 10-Q's credit-facility note, which states the $45m term loan carried at $44,323k and the minimum-availability covenant of the greater of $30,000k and 10% of the gross borrowing base - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001132105/000119312526253546/spwh-20260502.htm (2026-06-02). Separate wire confirmation of the extension: https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/sportsmans-warehouse-extends-and-restructures-key-credit-facilities

searched_and_found_nothing: Nasdaq minimum-bid-price / delisting angle from the sweep note: closed as a non-issue. No 8-K disclosing any Nasdaq correspondence, the baseline's 52w low implies the stock has never traded below $1 (spot $1.185, only 5.8% above the low), and on >$1.2bn of revenue SPWH clears the Nasdaq Global Market total-assets/total-revenue continued-listing standard regardless of a $45m market cap. https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001132105&type=8-K
No 8-K of any kind since 2026-06-24 (items 1.01/2.03/9.01, the refinancing). No pre-announcement, no covenant amendment, no management change, no impairment notice in the 10 weeks before the print.

Insider activity: exactly one Form 4 since 5 June - 2026-08-20, CFO Jennifer Fall Jung, 20,580 shares at $1.16, transaction code F (shares withheld for RSU vesting tax). No open-market purchase or sale, no cluster. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001132105/000178454026000006/form4-08202026_040801.xml
Short interest 1.23m shares, 3.41% of float, 2.6 days to cover - no squeeze or crowded-short mechanics to amplify a surprise. https://fintel.io/ss/us/spwh

A story served by search as current, headlined 'Sportsman's Warehouse Closing 23 Doors, Selling 15 Others' with ~2,600 employees affected, is dated 16 March 2009 and describes a 67-store company. Discarded. https://sgbonline.com/sportsmans-warehouse-closing-23-doors-selling-15-others/

Job-board postings (11 US openings on Glassdoor, seasonal hunting-buyer roles open to 30 Sep 2026) could not be date-anchored against any prior count, so no signal either way. https://www.glassdoor.com/Jobs/Sportsman-s-Warehouse-Jobs-E38562.htm

Could not quantify the suppressor/NFA tailwind: SPWH has sold suppressors online with Silencer Central fulfilment since 12 March 2025 (https://www.silencercentral.com/blog/sportsman-warehouse-suppressor-sales/) and NFA checks are up 108-177% YoY, but no SPWH disclosure sizes the channel and the economics are drop-ship, so I left it out of the findings rather than guess.

Company store locator (sportsmans.com/stores) and Fast Company both returned HTTP 403 - could not independently verify current store count or the status of the ~5 underperforming closures management said would happen after the holiday season.

No peer print lands before SPWH on the same May-July quarter: Smith & Wesson reports fiscal Q1 (quarter ended 31 July 2026) only on 3 September 2026, i.e. two days after. https://ir.smith-wesson.com/news-releases/news-release-details/smith-wesson-brands-inc-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial

No tariff commentary at all in the 2 June 2026 Q1 call transcript, and no quarter-to-date comp disclosure beyond a qualitative remark that June would be one of the largest months on Father's Day demand - so no company-sourced Q2 number exists to anchor against.
The 27 May 2026 8-K (items 5.02/5.07) is only an equity-plan amendment and routine annual-meeting results - no reverse split proposal, no share authorisation increase, no executive departure.
baseline_tension: The baseline has no measured skew and no implied move (23 contracts of open interest), so its 'what is priced' is inferred purely from a +3.04% 20-day drift - and my main finding cuts directly against that drift, because the three sector datapoints that support it (Olin 30 Jul, July NICS 5 Aug, Ruger 7 Aug) all landed inside that window and the tape did not respond, with the entire 20-day gain concentrated in the last five days as ordinary pre-earnings positioning; the one place I agree with the price is the gross-margin lap, which is why my net number is a quarter of the 14.1% expected move rather than a directional call on it.
